I want to know whether there is a permission in Islam to purchase a car on Installments. As per my knowledge, under installment scheme, you are supposed to pay the actual cost fixed intrest per month. But the cost is predecided by the bank for eg. if the vehicle cost is 4 lakhs, and if you are paying the installments in 3 years, bank will calculate the intrest and give you the final figure of 5.5 lakhs. So the cost of the car is 5.5 lakhs for you, which you are supposed to pay in 3 years. But if you change your plan of making payment in 4 years, then the total value of car will increase. So Please let me know whether we can purchase a car on installment. I can not buy a car by paying entire amount in cash, and car is very important for me to buy. Will be thankful to you for your advise. 2156 views Q. instalmment transaction 2251 views Q. AM I REQUIRED TO PAY THE ARREAS AS DEMANDE BY MR. AZHARUDDIN? 1794 views Q. I am a member of the managing committee of the building society in which we reside. The society comprises of 33 members, mostly muslims. We have got advertisement hoardings on the terrace through which, we generate good revenue. Every year we give gifts to all society members in the form of eatables etc. This year we decided to gift dry fruits. All the managing committee members went to the market to purchase the dry fruits for and on behalf of all the society members. After purchasing the dry fruits one of the managing committe members requested for some personal gift from the shop keeper. As the purchase was a huge amount, the shopkeeper gifted all the managing committee members some chocolates which they kept for personal use. I did not object at that time, but later decided that i would give the gift away in sadkah from the society's side and requested the other members to do the same. They all refused to give the choclates away. I told them three times but they still kept for personal use. Please tell me: Is keeping the gift allowed, when we went to purchase material for the society? How can we take personal favors from the shopkeeper? 2. Is giving it away in sadkah correct? Please reply at the earliest. 1487 views Q. I want to buy a plot from a plotting scheme i.e. provides installments. The total price of plot is 150,000 Rupees and advance is 15000 then 30 months schedule. There is not penalty charges. But no confirmation of re-pricing. Is is permissible to buy or not? 1896 views Q. Is it permissible to work as a Computer Auditor in a bank for experience and better financial stability? 1730 views Q. Currently there is a difference of opinion regarding what is known as ?Islamic Banking.? There are some ulama that are of the opinion that this type of banking and the services that they provide are halaal and a practicing Muslim should have not fear and fully take advantage of the variety of services being offered by these same banks. On the other hand there are a group of scholars that aver that this type of banking is no different than regular commercial non Islamic banks. The only differences being in the terminology, but the actual transactions fall into the category of riba. Our question to the ulama ikram is: in the opinion of your darul iftaa, which group is correct, as both can not be correct in this case. Please explain your fatwa completely which will eliminate the doubts in the minds of the common people. 2588 views Q. answer: Transactions & Dealings >> Other Transactions Question ID: 28552 Country: Pakistan Title: Giving out any residential place or any shop on rent is the reflection of the business of interest in its concept. Is it right or wrong? please elaborate with reference to Quran and Hadith. Question: Giving out any residential place or any shop on rent is the reflection of the business of interest in its concept. Is it right or wrong? please elaborate with reference to Quran and Hadith. Answer ID: 28552 Posted on: Sep 1, 2020 Bismillah hir-Rahman nir-Rahim ! (Fatwa: 29/25/L=1432) If the exchange of rupees is with rupees then dealing with difference is called interest. If there are rupees on one side and goods on the other side or any benefit, then the definition of interest does not apply to it. Hence, it is lawful to give the house or shop on rent definitely and there is no doubt of interest in it. Allah (Subhana Wa Ta'ala) knows Best Darul Ifta, Darul Uloom Deoband, India
